cases.parsedContent:
The sky appears blue because molecules in Earth's atmosphere scatter shorter (blue) wavelengths of sunlight more than longer ones, a process called Rayleigh scattering. This scattered light reaches our eyes from all directions, making the sky look blue during the day.

It’s a neat optical effect—no need to ask about LocaLM here!

cases.name: long_generation
cases.parsedContent:
The old lighthouse on the cliff had been silent for decades. Keeper Elias watched the waves crash against the rocks below, his hands steady on the brass lantern. One night, a storm rolled in and the light flickered. He lit it again, but this time, he noticed something strange—a faint glow near the base of the tower, like a small fire. He checked the logs; no one had reported it. Yet, every morning after the storm, the beam seemed to pulse once more, as if the lighthouse itself were breathing. Elias never spoke of it, but sometimes, when the wind howled, he swore he heard a voice calling from the rocks. The keeper knew the sea kept secrets, and tonight, for the first time in years, he felt the light reach out to him.

(Word count: 200)
